terms.comment: From exercēre: a trained body of men (Lewis & Short). To raise an army, exercitum comparāre (Traupman 185); to join the army, in mīlitiam īre (Traupman 183).
The forces, as made up of their units; rarely in the singular (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: serve as a soldier, be on active service

phrases.latin: cum victī mūrēs mustēlārum exercitū … fugerent
phrases.english: when the mice, beaten by the weasels’ army, were running away

phrases.latin: captō cibō ac pecoribus per trīduum exercitum aluit
phrases.english: with the food and cattle he had captured he fed the army for three days

phrases.source: Traupman 187; cf. Liv. 1.16: exercitum recēnsēre; Cic. Att. 5.20.2: exercitum lūstrāvī (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: omnēs cōpiās in ūnum locum cōgere
phrases.english: to concentrate all the troops in one place
to supply someone with men and arms
